newsitem.title: FRANCE: French probe new clue into murder of British girl.
newsitem.headline: French probe new clue into murder of British girl.

text.p: French police probing the murder of a British schoolgirl in France in July said on Sunday they were searching for a man said to have sexually assaulted another British teenager in the same area hours before.
Investigators said an unidentified man entered the bedroom of three schoolgirls at a holiday centre in Saint-Lunaire, Brittany, on the night of July 17-18 and assaulted one.
The man fled after the two other girls woke up. The assaulted girl's clothing was torn off and her face bruised.

A few hours later, 13-year-old Caroline Dickinson was found dead in her bed in a room she was sharing with four other girls in a youth hostel at Pleines-Fougeres, 50 km (30 miles) away. She had been raped and strangled.

The girls in Saint-Lunaire reported the incident to their teachers, who kept it quiet for fear that a police investigation would prevent the group from catching a ferry home the next day. They later told British police.
The French magistrate investigating the Dickinson murder, Gerard Zaug, has ordered gendarmes in Saint-Lunaire to investigate the incident.

Frenchman Patrice Pade, arrested soon after the killing, was released after DNA genetic tests showed he could not have committed the rape. French police said he withdrew an earlier confession to the murder.
Genetic tests on teachers, youth hostel employees and Dickinson's male classmates from Launceston Community College in Cornwall also proved negative.
Checks carried out in Switzerland and Italy on all those staying in the hostel at the time also found nothing.
